observation.visible_scene: A metallic four-arm spinner (central ball-bearing ring with four cylindrical end weights joined by brass/gold connector blocks) rests flat on top of a black rectangular pedestal against a plain white background. The camera is stationary; the pedestal and background do not move.
visible_changes: The spinner rotates slowly about its central vertical axis: the arms shift between diagonal (X-like) and more horizontal (cross-like) orientations relative to the camera across the frames.
A small dark notch/marker on the bearing ring moves around the upper portion of the ring, tracking the rotation.
The end weights and brass blocks slide laterally and change apparent spacing as the body turns, while the object's height and contact with the pedestal stay essentially constant.
Specular highlights on the polished metal surfaces shift as orientation changes.
The motion is continuous and gradual throughout the excerpt, with no visible onset, impact, or completion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the spinner was set in motion (no operator or initial spin is shown).
Whether the rotation continues, slows, or stops after the last frame.
The state of the spinner before the first frame.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation direction and speed are hard to confirm because the bearing marker's position is ambiguous between frames.
Small apparent vertical shifts of the arms may be perspective/tilt rather than true wobble.
Whether the brass connectors or end weights move independently of the central ring is not resolvable from these frames.
